name: RfOne Mk2 RF sensor (DroneShield)
description: Passive, non-emitting RF direction finder for UAS control and video links. Four units give 360 deg; multiple sites triangulate a position. DroneShield publishes no detection range, so the 5 km ring is a planning figure.

rangeAccuracyM.note: A single-site RF direction finder measures bearing, not range; not established by the public record.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of every sourced RF sensor regardless of role: lib-titan 1, lib-rf360 5, lib-wingman 30; median 5 deg. The role-restricted set (early-warning) holds only the body-worn Wingman, whose ±30° is a signal-strength sector indication and not comparable with a mast-mounted multi-element direction finder.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Two-dimensional RF direction finding gives no elevation; not established by the public record.

receiverSensitivityDbm.note: Planning factor, 2.4 GHz band, channel-integrated: kTB for a 10 MHz OcuSync-class channel (-104 dBm) plus a 12 dB receiver noise figure (Narda SignalShark C-UAS application note) gives -92 dBm, recorded as -90 dBm. DroneShield publishes no sensitivity; the RfOne product URL redirects to a portfolio page today.

geolocationMinNodes.condition: four 90° sector antennas give a sector bearing; 'deploying multiple RfOne MKII sensors ... enables triangulation'; two sites is the cross-bearing minimum
geolocationMinNodes.source: Army Technology, DroneShield RfOne MkII long-range sensors for Australia
